issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Stock class (and instruct students to use a final Stock stock attribute and static methods that manage Stock), but the template repository provides an Inventory class implementing the needed stock behavior while Stock.java is empty. The solution also uses Inventory as the shared stock (SealSaloon declares a static Inventory stock). This name/type mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students: they are told to work with Stock but the template does not provide an implemented Stock, preventing a straightforward implementation following the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across artifacts. Either (A) replace Inventory with Stock in the template (rename Inventory.java to Stock.java and update references), or (B) update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock. Alternatively, provide a Stock class in the template that delegates to Inventory (or extends it) so students can implement SealSaloon using the Stock type as described. Ensure the constructor signatures and public methods match the UML (add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock).

issues.description: The problem statement consistently refers to a 'Stock' class (and instructs students to implement a final Stock field in SealSaloon), while the provided template and solution code use an 'Inventory' class implementing the same methods (add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock). Additionally an empty Stock.java file exists in the template, increasing the chance of confusion. This mismatch between the conceptual name in the problem ('Stock') and the actual class name in the code ('Inventory') can mislead students about where to implement or look for stock-related functionality.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the Inventory class (and its files/usages) to Stock in the template and solution, or update the problem statement and diagram to refer to Inventory instead of Stock. Also remove or populate the empty Stock.java in the template to avoid confusion.
